title: A Naive Song
text: “Motoyasu-san, Fleon wants to see a little more of the play that was showing in this town the other day.”

Fleon-chan had apparently gone to watch an outdoor performance being put on in Zeltoble. From what I gathered, it was something called a Hero Show, a program that past heroes and the like had helped popularize.
“Understood. Let us go see it later, I say.”
“Thank you very much. Yuki-san, why don’t you come along with Motoyasu-san too?”
“Eh, yes! Yuki shall also accompany Motoyasu-sama.”
“Is Yuki-chan also interested in the performance, I wonder?”
“If anything, Yuki prefers races, but she does want to see the play.”
Understood!
“Go, go, hero, bearing everyone’s hopes in your hands, ride over the wave that leads to ruin—”

It seemed that in Zeltoble these days, programs of that sort had begun trending, born out of hopes pinned on heroes in the face of the terror of the Waves. And so, there stood Fleon-chan, singing away in high spirits. Filolial-sama joined in as well. Perhaps thanks to Elephant’s education, Filolial-sama had taken to harmonizing whenever someone sang, turning it into something rather operatic.
Now then. I figured Fleon-chan’s sensors would surely react to Itsuki, so I decided to keep an eye on the situation, indeed.
“Look, seems like a Filolial you might get along with has shown up. Why not try talking to her? I bet you could even have a chat with someone like Rishia-san.”
Itsuki, cool as anything, was making small talk with Rabbit Guy.
“I hear she’s the flying type of Filolial, though…”
“Well, if you’re the one riding her, appearing as a rabbit won’t exactly cut it—I’d recommend riding in human form properly. Maybe strike some sort of sentai pose, like Kuro-san or Rafumi-san do?”
“I don’t know if I’d go that far.”
“Still, it seems like every single rabbit ends up paired with a Filolial.”
Thwack—Itsuki kicked Rabbit Guy’s leg.
“That wasn’t me, was it? Please don’t kick me. Also, Filolials have been known to eat usapils alive, you know. You really do need to be careful about size, or it could get dangerous.”
“Is that so? Then how about this: the fate of a usaunny is to be devoured by the Filolial it loves, and die that way?”
“Apparently that guy has a weakness for corrupted Filolials or something. I heard he couldn’t refuse Luna-san’s request and ended up turning Sword Hero into an inult.”
“Now that’s useful information. I wonder how one might go about corrupting a Filolial.”
“Please stop. I’ll be the one who gets killed for telling you that.”
“Itsuki, what did you think of Fleon-chan’s song, I wonder?”

The plan was that, after tripping out a little, he’d awaken to true justice and the two would grow close, indeed. According to Itsuki from the previous loop, apparently it rings in your head, or the sound sticks with you like some kind of phantom noise.
“It’s a rather naive song. Fitting for someone at his level, don’t you think?”

That reaction—rather dull, wasn’t it? Whether they’d grow close remained to be observed further. And so, once Fleon-chan’s debut was over, I kept watch for a while, but there was no sign of any particular closeness developing between Itsuki and Fleon-chan. So I decided to ask Fleon-chan directly.
“Fleon-chan, Fleon-chan.”
“Yes, what is it, Motoyasu-san?”
“What do you make of Itsuki, I wonder?”
“Itsuki-san? Fleon thinks he’s acting on a sense of purpose different from the justice Fleon feels—more like, he carries his own particular brand of justice.”

Oh? She didn’t call it a twisted justice, nor did she call him a kindred spirit who sympathized with Fleon’s justice? And she showed no sign of resonating with Fleon-chan’s song either. Strange, wasn’t it?

“More than that, what’s been catching Fleon’s interest lately is Ren-san, the one Kuro-san seems fond of. Truthfully, Fleon can feel it, practically buzzing off him—that frustration of wanting to do justice but feeling too embarrassed to!”
I see, indeed.

“Say, Kuro, lately Fleon’s been curious about the Assassin of Midnight, Bloody Lith, you know? Rather than that form, wouldn’t it be nice if he acted in human shape—wearing an inconspicuous black outfit, fighting against the dark forces, the Dark Empire?”
Hmm? Was Kuro-chan taking an interest in Itsuki now? What in the world was going on here?
“Kuro-chan. What about Ren, I wonder?”

“Hmm, well, he’s cool and all, but he doesn’t really play with me much anymore. Whenever Iwa’s in trouble he comes running right away to help, you know? Ever since he started playing with the Dark Swordsman, Imitation, he’s changed.”

Ah, indeed, Ren had gotten into the habit of turning to Father for advice whenever something came up. Originally, whenever Kuro-chan latched onto him, he’d ask Father for help, but perhaps he’d grown so dependent on it that he’d dropped considerably on Kuro-chan’s sensor radar.
“Fu…”
“Ah, the Dark Swordsman—!”
And off Kuro-chan dashed, running toward Rafumi, who was disguised as Ren.
“Hey! How long are you gonna stay in my form?! At least turn back while you’re here!”
By the way, let me confirm once again—this was happening right around Zeltoble’s base of operations, indeed.
“That’s none of your business.”
“When we’re standing next to each other, people point at me and ask if I’m the fake! That’s exactly what happened to me the other day—I got mistaken for the impostor!”
And so began the back-and-forth between Ren and Rafumi. Well, Rafumi did tend to go around in a form that amplified Ren’s handsomeness by quite a margin. The outfit was rather flashy too.
“Boo.”
Kuro-chan lodged a mild protest against Ren looking so uncool like that.
I decided to bring this matter up with Father. That night, I found him inside the circus tent compiling some documents, and called out to him.
“First of all, as a premise—I do think you should reflect a little more on how you’ve been treating Itsuki rather carelessly, on the assumption that Fleon-chan can just brainwash him and all.”

“But it is effective for persuading a version of Itsuki who’s hard to reconcile with. Once things break down, if the loop resets, talking to him often does no good at all. So then, is turning him into a riska once more and having him experience torture the optimal solution, I wonder?”
“Well… I get what you’re saying, but…”
“Indeed, Bow Hero, once he’s convinced of his own justice, becomes troublesome, nano. Probably annoying enough that even Rafumi would agree, nano.”
“So Gaelion-chan agrees too, huh.”
Seizing the opportunity, Rival butted right in to join the conversation. Go home, I say!
“Even so, is that really the only method, though?”

“Gaelion has had to clean up after the ruin that comes at the end of Bow Hero’s rampages before, so Gaelion has every right to say so, nano. Like in this loop… in the very first loop Gaelion ever met Naofumi in, Bow Hero rampaged and broke down just like this, and in the end, after all his failures, he fell into corruption and died of sickness, nano.”
If that fate could easily be avoided, then it was a necessary measure, Rival argued back to Father.

“Hmm… seems like Itsuki really is difficult to handle. I do hope this loop’s Itsuki finds some peace… but somehow, right now, Itsuki seems convinced he won’t die a decent death no matter what, and he’s trying to drag himself down into darkness on his own—that part where he won’t spare himself in order to save whoever’s in front of him…”

“From what Gaelion’s heard, it sounds like he’s stopped hesitating to stain his hands with blood for the sake of protecting someone. Like, no matter how much blood and mud he has to wade through, he’ll do it for the sake of achieving his goal—and that’s a bit different from the justice Fleon holds up, it seems, nano.”
Fleon-chan, if anything, was more the sentai hero type. She preferred good triumphing over evil, plain and simple.

“The fact that Kuro-chan is reacting to Itsuki probably means he’s become the dark-hero type. Maybe it’s because their inner landscapes, their ideals, are different now, so he and Fleon-chan just aren’t on the same wavelength anymore?”
“He originally preferred operating without standing out, but it’s hard to tell the difference, nano.”
“Hmm… a masked hero and a dark hero are similar, but they’re a bit different, you know.”
Father swiftly jotted something down and explained it to Rival and me using notes.
